text:
Keiko Tan: quick report — saw duplicate side-effects in the onboarding sampleapp when a token refresh happened during a tight 429 retry window. single user click, two webhooks.

Marcus Lee: thanks — do you have a tiny repro?

Keiko Tan: minimal: start sampleapp locally, click `confirm`, run `./scripts/rotate_creds.sh` within the first backoff, set jitter=0 for determinism. logs show first req got 429 then 200, and a resumed replay also applied side-effect. snippet: `2026-03-26T22:11:01Z req=zz1 status=429 -> backoff -> token rotated -> req=zz1 status=200 side_effect applied -> req=zz1_retry status=200 side_effect applied`

Olga Ivanova: sounds like Idempotency-Key was dropped when the client rebuilt headers after refresh. which SDK?

Keiko Tan: node sampleapp v0.12.0 with node-sdk v0.11. Default node behavior rebuilt the request and omitted Idempotency-Key in the resumed attempt. go/python preserved it.

Marcus Lee: actionable: (1) SDKs must persist Idempotency-Key (and optionally X-Correlation-Id) across refresh/resume; (2) enable jitter=true by default for 429/backoff to reduce synchronized replays; (3) sampleapp and server should have a short configurable dedupe window (default 8s).

Olga Ivanova: agree. also add a small chaos test to CI that flips creds during backoff and asserts single side-effect. and add a short doc note in quickstart: "If you rotate tokens while requests are in-flight, ensure Idempotency-Key survives refresh."

ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-1500 "persist idempotency in node resume path" and queued CI job devex/sampleapp#replay-chaos

Keiko Tan: pushed repro branch `devex/replay-guard-node`. will follow up with PR for the node SDK and sampleapp changes.

Marcus Lee: will run a cross-sdk check after PRs land. also add telemetry `sdk.replayed_request.count` to detect duplicates in prod.

Keiko Tan: thanks all — will watch CI and remove jitter=0 from docs after we validate. :thumbsup:
